pr_title: Resolve runtime java via Gradle tool chain provider
pr_body:
Using gradle toolchain support in gradle requires refactoring how the composite build is composed. 
We added three toolchain resolver
1. Resolver for resolving defined bundled version from oracle as openjdk
2. Resolve all available jdks from Adoption
3. Resolve archived Oracle jdk distributions. 

We should be able to remove the JdkDownloadPlugin altogether without having that in place, but we'll do that in a separate PR.

Fixes #95094
pr_comments: We have some tests left that fail due to gradle toolchain support lacking well configuration cache behavior. see https://gradle-enterprise.elastic.co/s/fx2ra3p5l4rfc/tests/:build-tools-internal:integTest/org.elasticsearch.gradle.internal.test.rest.RestResourcesPluginFuncTest/restResources%20does%20nothing%20when%20there%20are%20no%20tests?focused-exception-line=0-23&top-execution=1
Are we intending to backport this?

issue_context.title: Passing `runtime.java` system property should auto-provision runtime JDK
issue_context.body: We already have some logic in `elasticsearch.runtime-jdk-provision.gradle` to auto-provision a runtime when no explicit one has been defined either via `RUNTIME_JAVA_HOME` or `-Druntime.java`. The `runtime.java` system property currently expects a major version (i.e. `20`) and then maps that to an environment variable `JAVA{version}_HOME` to find the actual JDK. We should do this automatically for folks by simply downloading an appropriate JDK based on the major version passed via `runtime.java` we can reuse the existing JDK download plugin or even the Gradle toolchain support for this.

review_comments: Do we want to keep the `JAVAX_HOME` environment variables at all? I'm leaning towards removing it entirely if we are auto-resolving things. That way at least it's consistent and we can remove the logic and documentation for this.

We could, but I would not want to do that in this PR. I wonder if there would be a downside in CI environments as the java runtimes are part of the image. We would probably need to change our gradle cache filling to also resolve required toolchains we test against.
We don't use this feature in CI at all. In CI we explicitly set `RUNTIME_JAVA_HOME` to the specific JDK we are intending to test.
In what cases do we specifically request an Oracle vendor JDK where the equivalent adoptium one won't work?
I thought this would be neat if we want to test against oracle jdks specifically in certain situations.
Not really. Just matching to ordering of the parameter.  🤓
The existing logic doesn't work with the reworked composition setup

Keep in mind that when the bundled JDK is an initial release, the version string is something like `20+3` and then subsequent patches are `20.0.1+6` or similar. I don't think this will work in the former case as it would report `20+3` as the major version.
This works with 20+3 and 20+36 as I tested it with the initial 20 release
